scorecards.inningsCommentary: Bangladesh commenced their first innings at Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium, aiming to set an imposing baseline total. Mohammad Mithun anchored the innings with a resolute 63, providing backbone against a probing bowling attack while middle-order partnerships consolidated the position. Pakistan's bowling response was spearheaded by Shaheen Afridi (5/50), who generated sustained pressure and triggered critical breakthroughs to prevent runaway scoring. Concluding at 233/10 (82.5 ov), Bangladesh posted a competitive total, ensuring a closely matched contest.

scorecards.inningsCommentary: Pakistan began their reply under scoreboard pressure, tasked with responding to Bangladesh's opening innings total. The centerpiece of the innings was a brilliant 143 from Babar Azam, complemented by a commanding 137-run stand between Asad Shafiq and Babar Azam that absorbed bowling hostility and accelerated the scoring rate to 3.61 RPO. Bangladesh's bowling response was spearheaded by Rubel Hossain (4/111), who generated sustained pressure and triggered critical breakthroughs to prevent runaway scoring. Reaching 445/10 (122.5 ov), Pakistan's innings completed the first-innings exchange (212 Runs (Pakistan)), shaping the strategic contours for the second half of the Test.

scorecards.inningsCommentary: Entering the third innings with the match balance in flux, Bangladesh sought to extend their lead and set a decisive fourth-innings target. The centerpiece of the innings was a brilliant 41 from Mominul Haque, complemented by a commanding 71-run stand between Mominul Haque and Najmul Shanto that absorbed bowling hostility and accelerated the scoring rate to 2.68 RPO. Pakistan's bowling response was spearheaded by Naseem Shah (4/26), who generated sustained pressure and triggered critical breakthroughs to prevent runaway scoring. Bangladesh's total of 168/10 (62.2 ov) closed their second innings, cementing a formidable target and transferring immense pressure onto the opposition.

summaryTab.matchCommentary:
The Test match at Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium commenced with high tactical intensity as Bangladesh posted 233/10 (82.5 ov) in their opening innings. In response, Pakistan countered with 445/10 (122.5 ov), setting the stage for a compelling contest of tactical endurance. Early sessions tested batting resolve against disciplined seam movement, with both attacks striving to gain the upper hand on a developing surface.

The defining turning point arrived during Collapse: Lost 10 Wickets for 129 Runs, which irrevocably altered the trajectory of the match. As the match progressed through its pivotal middle stages, Babar Azam delivered a masterclass for Pakistan (143 Runs), absorbing intense pressure and tilting the momentum decisively. Crucial partnership stands and incisive bowling spells broke the opposition's resistance, shifting the control share (Pakistan 73%) and allowing Pakistan to dictate terms heading into the decisive sessions.

Entering the final innings, Bangladesh faced an uphill battle under unrelenting scoreboard pressure. Pakistan's bowling unit, bolstered by Haris Sohail (75 Runs & 2 Wkts), maintained relentless discipline and attacked the stumps relentlessly. Wicket clusters in the closing sessions dismantled any remaining resistance, sealing Pakistan won by innings & 44 runs in comprehensive fashion.

Verdict: Pakistan's triumph was built on superior pressure absorption, clinical execution during critical moments, and the ability to dominate key sessions. While Bangladesh produced fighting phases, Pakistan won the pivotal turning points and sustained higher tactical control across all five days to emerge as deserved victors.
